decisions.problem: How to keep lane tabs clean while preserving sessions for skill-cost accounting and resume.
options: Move finished panes to an archive tab
Copy session files to a local archive, then close the tab
decisions.selected: dispatch.sh opens one tab per lane (label = lane name, --no-focus) and records dispatch.json. archive.sh copies the lane's Pi session dirs (keyed by the worktree cwd) and its agy conversation (.db plus the brain/<id> transcript JSONL, found through cache/last_conversations.json) into ~/skill-heaven-wt/sessions/<lane>/, saves the final terminal buffer, writes archive.json, and closes the tab. Originals stay in place, so a lane can still be resumed. The archive is local only, never committed (transcripts are excluded from the repo by policy).

decisions.problem: Security limit raised by a side agent and confirmed against P1's own method. MCP elicitation (channel 1) delivers whatever is typed into the terminal to the server. In P1, a worker agent answered the elicitation prompt with herdr pane send-text, and the server received a normal accept that nothing distinguished from a person. Any process that can write to the terminal can do the same: every lane here (herdr socket), and a Skill Ultra session's own model when it has a shell tool and its terminal sits in herdr or tmux (HERDR_SOCKET_PATH / TMUX in its environment); for example, a parallel shell call issued beside the campaign call.
options: Keep channel 1, state plainly what it is not, disclose terminal multiplexing at decision time, and require the real proof decision to be made where no agent can inject input
Invent a nonce or challenge (rejected: an agent can read the pane as easily as type into it)
decisions.selected: Keep channel 1 as the selected channel (it still keeps the model out of the tool path, and no channel on this harness authenticates a person), but: (1) the P1 record and the U3 evidence say that channel 1 is terminal input, not authentication, the same class of boundary as channels 2 and 3 and the steering brand; (2) U3's operator path records, with each operator entry, an attribution field 'terminal-input, unauthenticated' plus whether the server's environment shows a multiplexer (HERDR_ENV/HERDR_SOCKET_PATH/TMUX), and the decisions render discloses it; (3) U9's real operator decision is made by the founder in a terminal no agent controls (outside herdr and tmux, or a pane whose socket no running agent can reach), and PROOF.md says which; (4) no test fixture keystroke is ever recorded as a person's decision.
decisions.reason: Honest disclosure of a real boundary without inventing authentication the harness does not provide; it preserves invariant 4 (agent text cannot manufacture operator authority) in the proof, where it matters.
decisions.authority: Plan section 5.3 ('says plainly what it is not'); security invariants 4 and 15; directive section 8 (never forge an approval)
decisions.terra: U3 review and the final integration review must check items 1-4
decisions.risk: In product use, a session whose model has shell access inside a multiplexer can approve its own charter. The disclosure makes that visible; it does not prevent it. A stronger channel would need a harness feature that does not exist on 2.1.325.

decisions.problem: Implement FD-11: safeguarded default, an unadvertised opt-in for multiplexed approvals, and a probe of auto mode's classifier.
decisions.selected: (1) Default: an elicitation accept grants operator authority only when the server's environment shows no multiplexer (HERDR_ENV, HERDR_SOCKET_PATH, TMUX). Otherwise the decisions step fails closed at DECISIONS with a plain message. (2) Advanced opt-in: the person sets an env var themselves before launching the session (name fixed in vocabulary.ts, e.g. SKILL_ULTRA_MULTIPLEXED_DECISIONS=accept-risk). It is documented only in an advanced or evidence note, never in the README, site, command help or skill text. Under opt-in, every operator entry records attribution 'terminal-input, unauthenticated', multiplexed:true and optIn:true, and the decisions render and status show it. (3) Safeguard inside the opt-in: the elicitation form asks the person to type the charter's short digest, shown in the prompt, so a blind or replayed injection does not match. This is disclosed as friction, not authentication. (4) Probe P1d measures auto mode's classifier against a self-approval attempt, and U3 records the result per mode.
decisions.reason: Matches FD-11: a safe default for ordinary users, nothing advertised, and advanced multiplexer users keep working. Terra's critical finding is answered by the default fail-closed plus an explicit, recorded, person-set opt-in.
decisions.terra: U3 review must verify the default fail-closed, the opt-in recording, and that no user-facing surface advertises the opt-in
decisions.risk: An agent that launches sessions could set the env var itself. The opt-in is recorded on every entry so this is visible after the fact. The OS-level keystroke-injection residual stays disclosed.
